definitions.explanation: A verbal warning or reprimand intended to correct behavior or prevent mistakes.
A guiding principle or moral drawn from experience, often passed down as wisdom.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}の{戒|いまし}めを{守|まも}る。
{上司|じょうし}から{厳|きび}しい{戒|いまし}めを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received a stern warning from my boss.

examples.japanese: {二度|にど}と{遅刻|ちこく}しないようにと{戒|いまし}めを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I was admonished not to be late again.

examples.japanese: この{話|はなし}は{良|よ}い{戒|いまし}めになる。
examples.english: This story serves as a good lesson.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{戒|いまし}めとする。
examples.english: To take past failures as a lesson.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}が{語|かた}った{戒|いまし}めの{言葉|ことば}を、{今|いま}でも{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
examples.english: I still treasure the words of wisdom my grandmother told me.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {戒|いまし}める (to warn, to admonish). Refers both to a warning given to correct someone and to a moral lesson or precept.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {戒|いまし}めを{受|う}ける: to receive a warning
- {戒|いまし}めを{守|まも}る: to heed a warning
- {戒|いまし}めとする: to take as a lesson
- {戒|いまし}めの{言葉|ことば}: words of admonition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {警告|けいこく}: official or formal warning, often about danger
- {忠告|ちゅうこく}: advice or counsel given out of concern
- {教訓|きょうくん}: moral lesson, often drawn from stories or experience

{戒|いまし}め has a more personal, moral tone compared to the more formal {警告|けいこく}, and overlaps with {教訓|きょうくん} in the sense of a lesson learned.
